rationale: Start with a broad mid-strength scouting gradient at moderate temperature to capture the full elution window, avoid truncation, and reveal whether peaks are compressed early, late, or across the whole gradient. This gives a strong first map of retention and critical pairs for later optimization.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the score is now limited only by last-peak time. Keep the same broad window and temperature but shorten the gradient one step to pull the last peak earlier while checking whether the closest pair stays above 1.5.

We are very close to the ideal score and the limiting pair is still just above the 1.5 threshold, so take one more step shorter in tG to try to bring the last peak under 10 min. This directly tests whether the critical pair can tolerate slightly steeper conditions.

The only lost score is the 6/7 pair, and shortening tG showed it is slope-sensitive while time is already below 10 min. Lowering temperature should modestly increase retention and can improve selectivity for that close pair without sacrificing too much run time.

Lowering T hurt selectivity badly, so test the opposite direction at the same fast gradient. If 45 C improves the critical middle cluster while keeping the last peak under 10 min, it could outperform the current best.

At 14 min and 40 C only one pair is sub-threshold, and temperature changes made selectivity worse, so the next lever is the phi window. Narrowing the gradient slightly while keeping the same tG makes the slope shallower and may recover the 6/7 resolution with only a small time penalty.

The narrower window improved the critical 6/7 pair while keeping the last peak under 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. This should further shallow the gradient around the eluting band and may push that pair to full resolution without incurring any time penalty.

At phi1 0.85 the mixture is fully resolved, so now the task is to reduce the small time penalty. Shortening tG by one step should pull the last peak back under 10 min while staying near the resolution boundary for the 6/7 pair.

The 12 min gradient at phi1 0.85 was too steep for the critical 6/7 pair, while phi1 0.90 at 14 min was close to ideal. Testing the intermediate combination should trade a little selectivity loss against faster elution and may beat the current best if the pair stays near or above 1.5.

The best region is clearly around phi1 0.85–0.90 at 40 C, and the critical 6/7 pair improves as the gradient is made shallower. Try phi1 0.85 with a longer tG to secure full resolution and map whether this window gives enough selectivity margin to support later fine time optimization.

The main unresolved cluster sits mid-gradient, while the earliest peaks have excessive spacing and do not need such a low starting strength. Raising phi0 should trim unneeded early gradient space, potentially pull the run slightly earlier, and may fine-tune selectivity around the critical 6/7 pair without changing overall steepness much.

Raising phi0 improved the score while keeping the last peak comfortably under 10 min, and narrowing phi1 previously improved the critical 6/7 pair. Combining those two favorable moves is the best chance to push that pair to full credit and reach CRF 1.000.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so the remaining objective is to find the shortest method that still preserves full resolution. Shorten tG one step from the optimum and test whether the critical 6/7 pair remains at or above 1.5.

Since shortening tG broke the critical pair, keep the proven window and slope but probe temperature around the optimum to see whether a small selectivity gain can create more margin while staying at CRF 1.000. A lower temperature may widen the 6/7 separation enough to make the method more robust.

35 C strongly worsened selectivity, so test the opposite temperature at the proven optimum window and slope. This checks whether 40 C is truly the selectivity maximum or whether a slightly higher T can retain CRF 1.000 with a bit more speed margin.

40 C is clearly optimal, so refine the gradient window around the successful method by slightly increasing phi0. This may compress the unneeded early space and shift the middle cluster into a more favorable part of the gradient while hopefully keeping the critical 6/7 pair above 1.5.

This new window gives full resolution with a bit more time margin than the earlier optimum, so test whether that margin is enough to shorten tG by one step. If the critical 6/7 pair survives, this would be a faster fully optimal method.

The 0.15–0.85 window is fully resolving with some margin, so narrow the high-organic end one more step to see if the critical pair gains selectivity while the last peak stays under 10 min. This explores whether the gradient can be trimmed more tightly around the actual elution window without losing full score.

Increasing phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 improved speed while keeping full resolution, so test one more step higher at the successful phi1 0.85 and tG 14. This could further shorten the run and still preserve the critical 6/7 pair above threshold.

We have two 1.000 methods at phi1 0.85 with phi0 0.10 and 0.15, and the latter gives slightly earlier elution. Expanding phi1 one step at phi0 0.15 tests whether this window can keep full resolution while moving the last peak a bit earlier than the current best.

The 0.15–0.80 window gave strong resolution margin for the critical pair but only a slight time penalty at 14 min, suggesting it may tolerate a shorter gradient. Testing 12 min here is the best remaining chance to find a faster fully resolved method than the current 1.000 conditions.

The optimum appears to sit very close to the resolution boundary for the 6/7 pair, so a slightly shallower version will map robustness around the winning method. This tests whether a modest increase in tG gives extra resolution margin while still remaining near the 10 min target.

Both phi0 0.10/phi1 0.85 and phi0 0.15/phi1 0.80 are near-optimal, so test the combined tighter upper end with the lower starting composition. This may keep the strong 6/7 resolution of phi1 0.80 while pulling the last peak back under 10 min.

With only two injections left and 40 C clearly optimal, probe the last untested adjacent high-end window around the winning phi0. This checks whether a slightly broader upper range can preserve full resolution while improving the last-peak time versus the current 1.000 methods.

For the final shot, test the only remaining nearby 14 min, 40 C window around the successful phi0 0.10–0.15 region that has not yet been explored. This closes the local map and checks whether the lower phi0 that gave 1.000 can pair with a broader upper end to retain full resolution while possibly offering a faster last peak.
